channel.title: Open Calls for Artists — Monographica
channel.description: Curated list of open calls for photographers and visual artists. Exhibitions, grants, residencies, and publications worldwide.

item.title: Images of the Shrub-Steppe 2026 · Boxx Gallery
item.description: Annual juried exhibit presented by Boxx Gallery and Cowiche Canyon Conservancy celebrating the shrub-steppe lands of Central Washington — the tenth Conservancy show at the Tieton gallery. Work in any medium made within the past five years and inspired by the shrub-steppe landscape is eligible, as long as it hasn't appeared in a previous edition; CaFE lists the call as regional to Washington. Accepted work may be shipped to arrive by August 27 or hand-delivered September 1, and must be for sale (35% gallery commission). Juried by photographer and 2022 Guggenheim Fellow Nancy Floyd. On view September 5–27, 2026, with Juror's, People's Choice, and Cowiche Canyon Conservancy awards of $100 each. — Deadline: July 31, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: Three $100 awards + Exhibition.

item.title: FL3TCH3R Exhibit 2026 — Socially & Politically Engaged Art
item.description: Thirteenth annual international juried exhibition of socially and politically engaged art, founded in memory of designer Fletcher H. Dyer and newly at home at Fischman Gallery in downtown Johnson City, Tennessee. All 2D, 3D, video, sound, and performance documentation is eligible, with photography as its own category; open worldwide to artists 18+. Juried by Jessica “JB” Burke of UNC Charlotte, with Best of Show, two Awards of Excellence, and a slate of named awards presented at the September 4 reception. On view August 7 – September 27, 2026; late entries accepted June 24–30 at a $45 fee. — Deadline: June 23, 2026. Fee: $40 for 3 works. Prize: Best of Show award + Exhibition.

item.title: 82nd Wabash Valley Exhibition · Swope Art Museum
item.description: Eighty-second edition of the Swope Art Museum's annual juried exhibition in downtown Terre Haute, running since 1944. Open to current or former residents of Indiana, Illinois, Kentucky, Michigan, Ohio, and Tennessee with original work in any medium completed 2024–2026 and not previously shown at the Swope. Juried by Mark Pascale, curator in the Department of Prints and Drawings at the Art Institute of Chicago. More than $10,000 in awards, from $100 Awards of Recognition to the Grand Prize, announced at the October 2 opening reception. On view October 2, 2026 – January 10, 2027. — Deadline: July 10, 2026. Fee: $40 (members free). Prize: $10,000+ in awards.

item.title: Baltic Open Submission 2026
item.description: BALTIC's all-comers exhibition returns for its third edition, with up to 100 works selected for a major group show at the Gateshead gallery from September 19, 2026 to May 2027. Open to anyone based in North East England — professional, self-taught, or hobbyist, individuals and collectives alike, working in any medium, with no exhibiting experience required. One work per artist, submitted as images via Submittable by 10am on June 16. Selection panel includes artists Laura Lancaster and Rachel Lancaster; selected artists notified August 6 and announced publicly August 20. — Deadline: June 16, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition at BALTIC.

item.title: OD Photo Prize 2026 · Open Doors Gallery
item.description: Sixth edition of Open Doors Gallery's annual open call for emerging photographic artists working within the first ten years of their practice. Open-themed and international — from documentary and street photography to collage, mixed media, and experimental lens-based work; collectives and duos welcome. Submit a project of 6–15 images with an artist statement. At least 20 shortlisted artists join a group exhibition in London in November–December 2026 (venue TBC), with works produced by the gallery and sold on a profit-share basis. The winner receives £2,000, an interview in 1000 Words Magazine, long-term mentorship, and an OD artist listing with an Artsy profile for at least a year. Additional awards include Judges' Picks, the InCadaqués Award — a solo presentation at the festival in Spain — and the AJ Page People's Choice Award. — Deadline: August 11, 2026. Fee: £17. Prize: £2,000 + Exhibition + Mentorship.

item.title: Underwater Awards Australasia 2026
item.description: Third edition of the underwater imaging competition run by DivePhotoGuide, Underwater Australasia, and UW Images. Nine categories — Sydney, Conservation, Australian, International Waters, Tough TG, Portfolio, Smartphone/Action Cam, the new Only Water, and a Reels video showcase — with around AU$70,000 in prizes spanning dive resort packages, underwater imaging equipment, and a photography drone. Open worldwide; images must be shot in the Australasian region, with exceptions for the International Waters and select categories. Winners are announced at the Go Diving Show ANZ in Sydney in September 2026, where finalist images are displayed as metal prints; honours include a Scuba Diver magazine cover story and publication in the 2027 Australian Marine Conservation Society calendar. Proceeds support environmental partners. — Deadline: July 19, 2026. Fee: $10/image. Prize: AU$70,000 prize pool.

item.title: ADEX Dugong Photo of the Year 2027
item.description: Conservation photography campaign from Asia Dive Expo (ADEX) and Asian Geographic spotlighting dugongs and their threatened seagrass habitats. Submit up to three images of dugongs in the wild or the underwater and coastal environments linked to them, each with a short story of 80–150 words; entrants also post their submission on Instagram with @AsiaDiveExpo added as collaborator. Free to enter. The grand prize winner is hosted at ADEX 2027 in Singapore with accommodation covered, receives a feature showcase, and is presented at the Blue Legacy Awards on April 11, 2027; shortlisted photographers are exhibited at ADEX 2027, featured online, and receive digital recognition. Public voting begins January 11, 2027. — Deadline: December 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Hosted stay at ADEX Singapore + Exhibition.

item.title: 12th Regional Juried Photography Exhibition · Rehoboth Art League
item.description: Twelfth annual juried photography exhibition at the Rehoboth Art League's historic campus in Henlopen Acres near Rehoboth Beach, Delaware, on view January 8 – February 7, 2027. Open to photographers living in Delaware, Pennsylvania, Maryland, New Jersey, Virginia, and Washington, D.C. — members and non-members alike. Submit up to 3 works created after January 2025; all work must be for sale, with a 65/35 artist/league split. Juried by Andre Wright Jr., who also awards $500, $250, and $150 prizes. Opening reception January 8, followed by a gallery talk with the juror on January 9. — Deadline: November 16, 2026. Fee: $45 ($25 members). Prize: $500 / $250 / $150 + Exhibition.

item.title: 2027 Solo and Group Exhibition Proposals · Rehoboth Art League
item.description: The Rehoboth Art League's Exhibitions Committee invites proposals for solo and group exhibitions in its 2027 gallery season at the League's campus in Henlopen Acres near Rehoboth Beach, Delaware. Open to members and non-members working in any media, including photography; artists who exhibited at RAL in 2024, 2025, or 2026 are not eligible. Solo applicants submit 5 works and groups 10, created no earlier than 2024, with an artist statement and CV. A limited number of proposals are accepted each year; selected artists are notified by August 31, 2026, and receive 65% of sales. — Deadline: July 27, 2026. Fee: $45 ($25 members). Prize: Solo or group exhibition.

item.title: Portfolio Platform 2026/2027 · Midwest Center for Photography
item.description: The Midwest Center for Photography's online series-portfolio program: selected photographers receive a six-month feature on the MWCP website from October 2026 through March 2027, presenting a thematic body of 10–20 images with an artist statement and biography as a virtual gallery experience. Work is evaluated on the strength of the series rather than individual images. Open internationally to all photographers; visitors can view and purchase photographs through the feature page (50% commission). — Deadline: July 31, 2026. Fee: $100/10 images. Prize: None listed.

item.title: Mini Maxi Print 2026 · Galleri Heike Arndt DK
item.description: Open call for professional graphic artists worldwide from Galleri Heike Arndt DK's Berlin space in Friedrichshain, for an exhibition of small and large-format print editions opening October/November 2026. Eligible techniques are editioned printmaking — lithograph, screen print, woodcut, etching, drypoint, linocut, photogravure and similar — in editions of at least 3; monoprints, inkjet and digital prints, and photo-based images without a physically worked plate are excluded. Submit 3–6 prints per section. Free to apply; selected artists pay a €40 exhibition fee plus shipping both ways, and works must remain available for the exhibition period plus 12 months. The gallery produces flyers and a poster featuring each artist. — Deadline: June 30, 2026. Fee: Free (€40 if selected). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: PRC Artist-in-Residence 2026
item.description: The Photographic Resource Center's Artist-in-Residence program gives two artists working in photography and lens-based media four weeks of dedicated studio space inside the PRC gallery, October 21 – November 22, 2026. Each resident gets exclusive use of half the gallery (about 400 sq ft), access to the darkroom, alternative process lab, and digital lab at Lesley University, a $500 stipend, weekly feedback meetings with the PRC Executive Director, and the opportunity to lead one public program. The residency culminates in a dual exhibition November 14–23 with a shared opening reception, artist talks, and professional documentation. Non-live-in: artists arrange their own housing, and there is no location requirement; collaborators may apply to share one slot. Fee $30 ($20 for PRC members). — Deadline: August 31, 2026. Fee: $30 ($20 members). Prize: Residency + $500 stipend + Exhibition.

item.title: Jentel Artist Residency — Winter/Spring 2027
item.description: Residency at Jentel, a working cattle ranch 20 miles southeast of Sheridan in Banner, Wyoming, for the Winter/Spring session running January 15 – May 7, 2027. Residents receive private accommodation, a separate individual studio, and a $300 stipend distributed in weekly increments to offset living expenses. Open to visual artists in all media — photography included — plus writers and composers. Applicants must be US residents (citizenship not required) aged 25 or over; full-time students are not eligible, and Wyoming residents have a streamlined application. Applications close September 15 at 12:00 noon MST. — Deadline: September 15, 2026. Fee: $30. Prize: Residency + $300 stipend.

item.title: Hambidge Center Residency — Spring 2027
item.description: Self-directed residencies of 2–8 weeks at the Hambidge Center's 600 forested acres in Rabun Gap, in the mountains of north Georgia, for the Spring session running mid-February through May 2027. Open to visual artists including photographers, plus writers, musicians, dancers, scientists, culinary artists, and arts administrators. Residents pay $300/week (the actual cost of $2,250/week is subsidized by the center); merit-based Distinguished Fellowships cover two weeks plus a $700 stipend, and limited financial-aid scholarships are available. Application fee $30, with waivers on request. Note: no cell service on campus and studios are offline — WiFi in communal spaces only. Applications open August 1 and close September 15, 2026. — Deadline: September 15, 2026. Fee: $30. Prize: Residency + Fellowship options.

item.title: Künstler*dorf Schöppingen Fellowship 2027
item.description: Residency fellowships at the Künstler*dorf (artists' village) in Schöppingen, Münsterland, Germany. Applications for the 2027 fellowships are open June 27 – August 31, 2026. Fellows live and work on site for two to six months, arranged by agreement and availability. Individual fellows receive €1,500 per month (minus roughly €100–200 for rent and operating costs); collectives — accepted since 2023 — receive €1,000 per person up to €3,000 total. Open worldwide to professional visual artists, authors, and composers with no restrictions on nationality or age. Juries assess the quality of previous work, the feasibility of the proposed project in Schöppingen, and contributions to the residency community. Not a production fellowship: there are no presentation obligations, though fellows may use the exhibition spaces. — Deadline: August 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €1,500/month stipend + 2–6 month residency.

item.title: 2026 Regional Fine Art and Photography Show · Lincoln Gallery
item.description: Annual juried regional show by the Thompson Valley Art League at its Lincoln Gallery in downtown Loveland, Colorado, running September 11 – October 1, 2026, with photography as a dedicated category alongside fine art media. Open to artists living in AK, AZ, CA, CO, HI, ID, KS, MT, ND, NE, NM, NV, OR, SD, TX, UT, WA and WY. Cash awards for Best of Show plus first and second place in each category. Enter via CaFE by July 8, 2026, 11:59 pm MDT. — Deadline: July 8, 2026. Fee: $45 (2 entries), $10 each additional. Prize: Cash awards + Exhibition.

item.title: Here & Now · Still In Street
item.description: Open call from London street photography collective Still In Street for Here & Now, a one-night exhibition at the Photobook Cafe, Leonard Circus, London, on August 20, 2026, 6–10pm, accompanied by a zine. Looking for candid, unstaged street photographs shot in London between 2020 and 2026 — no composites or AI-generated images. Submit up to 3 photographs by email (under 1MB each) with your name, Instagram handle, and a brief description; one image per photographer will be shown. Free to enter; a £20 printing fee applies to selected works, and selected photographers keep their print and receive a copy of the exhibition zine. — Deadline: June 24, 2026. Fee: Free (£20 if selected). Prize: Exhibition + Zine.

item.title: The Analog Forever Exhibit 2026 · LightBox Photographic Gallery
item.description: Fourth annual partnership exhibition between LightBox Photographic Gallery and Analog Forever Magazine, celebrating photography's analog roots. Open worldwide to any style or medium — the sole requirement is that the work includes at least one analog element in the creative process, whether it starts on film, passes through a hand process, or ends as an analog print. Platinum prints, cyanotypes, lumen prints, gelatin silver, three-dimensional objects and assemblage all welcome; the artist's hand must be evident. Juried by Michael Kirchoff, Editor-in-Chief of Analog Forever Magazine. Exhibition runs August 8 – October 7, 2026 at the gallery in Astoria, Oregon; accepted works due August 1. Fee $40 for up to 5 submissions, $60 for up to 10. — Deadline: July 5, 2026. Fee: $40–$60. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Lake Garda Photo Challenge · Comune di Sirmione
item.description: Season-long photo contest from the Sirmione Award for Photography, inviting images of Sirmione and the wider Lake Garda basin. Two main themes — Sirmione and Lake Garda — each award €1,500 first prize, €500 second, and a two-night stay in Sirmione for third. Up to three photographs may be entered across the main themes (any shooting date), plus an optional fourth for the bonus tracks Margins (nature reclaiming abandoned spaces) or In the Heart of the Night (low-light work), which carry hospitality prizes; a special award honors the area's historical and archaeological heritage. Flat €10 registration regardless of the number of photographs; reflex, compact and phone cameras admitted. — Deadline: October 31, 2026. Fee: €10. Prize: €1,500 + Sirmione stays.

item.title: 1839 Awards Photographer of the Year Contest
item.description: Flagship open-genre cycle of the 1839 Awards, recognizing creators working with the camera as an art form across 22 categories — from Abstract, Aerial and Architecture to Film/Analog, Photojournalism, Street and Wildlife. Over $4,000 in cash prizes plus international media exposure, a profile in the 1839 Artist Directory, published interviews in 1839 Magazine, online exhibition space, and entry into the People's Vote Awards. Open worldwide to professional and non-professional photographers; single images or series of 2–5. Early bird pricing through July 22, regular deadline August 19, extended final deadline September 16; winners announced October 28, 2026. — Deadline: September 16, 2026. Fee: $27–$50. Prize: $4,000.

item.title: Raccont'Arti: Contemporary Photography Award 2026 · Castelfiorentino Prize for the Arts
item.description: Free international award mapping the state of contemporary photography, promoted by Fondazione Teatro del Popolo, Ente Cambiano, Centro Culturale Cambio and the Municipality of Castelfiorentino in Tuscany. The 2026 theme is 'Beyond the visible: the image of absence' — absence as space-time stratification, mapping what remains when action subsides. Submissions are projects only (10–30 images) in documentary, artistic or hybrid approaches, in two categories: Open (€3,000) and Student (€500, for current students or graduates within the past year). Winners plus four finalists per category join a group exhibition at Centro Culturale Cambio, with exhibition production and award-ceremony accommodation fully covered by the Prize. — Deadline: October 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €3,000 + €500 student + Exhibition.

item.title: Liminal Magazine — Issue 2 · Phantasmal Gallery
item.description: Second issue of Liminal Magazine, Phantasmal Gallery's photo-book-style publication devoted to liminality, the uncanny, horror, surrealism and atmospheric strangeness. Open internationally to visual artists working in photography, painting, drawing, sculpture and fashion, alongside written pieces up to 1,500 words. Up to 6 works per artist, submitted by email with titles, mediums and an artist statement; accepted artists pay a £15 fee. Contributors receive a printed copy (postage included), features across the gallery's Instagram and TikTok channels, and circulation to a readership across the UK, Europe and North America. — Deadline: June 15, 2026. Fee: Free (£15 if accepted). Prize: Publication.

item.title: Rock, Paper, Scissors — Golden Duck Gallery
item.description: International open call themed around mixed media and pop art — physical and digital painting, photography, mixed media, sculpture and installation all welcome. Exhibition at Golden Duck Gallery in Budapest, September 1 – October 1, 2026, with digital showcases in New York, Vienna and Budapest. €500 prize fund including two €150 awards for Concept and Special Media. Free to submit up to 5 artworks; if accepted, exhibition fees are €60 for one work, €90 for two, €110 for three. Artists aged 14–25 exhibit free and compete for a special young artist prize. AI-created or co-created work must be marked. — Deadline: July 26, 2026. Fee: Free (€60–€110 if accepted). Prize: €500 prize fund.

item.title: Traveller's Art Fair 2026 — Golden Duck Gallery
item.description: Open-topic affordable art exhibition at Golden Duck Gallery in Budapest, August 4–29, 2026, aimed at work that appeals to the city's summer visitors. Photography, painting, mixed media, sculpture and installation accepted, with price caps of €450 for works under 60×60 cm and €1,000 under 100×100 cm. €500 prize fund with money prizes awarded by jury, plus special prizes announced at the opening; three Curator's Pick works exhibit free. Free to submit up to 5 artworks; €60 per accepted work for the four-week show. Works must arrive in Budapest ready to hang by July 31 at the artist's expense. AI-created or co-created work must be marked. — Deadline: June 28, 2026. Fee: Free (€60/work if accepted). Prize: €500 prize fund.

item.title: Arty Rat Magazine Open Call — July 2026
item.description: Summer open call from the Vienna-based independent art magazine for bold contemporary visual work worldwide — art, illustration and photography. Free to submit up to 6 works by online form or email; if selected, publishing options range from €35 (magazine publication) to €65 (magazine plus artist website page) and €100 (curatorial review or Vienna exhibition). Two artists are chosen for cover features, and one artist receives free participation in The Names Gallery group exhibition in Vienna. Selected artists get a digital magazine copy, printed page photos and an Instagram feature. — Deadline: July 1, 2026. Fee: Free (€35–€100 if accepted). Prize: Publication.

item.title: Louvre Unbound Magazine — Volumes 7 & 8 Open Call
item.description: International contemporary art magazine seeking visual artists worldwide for Volumes 7 and 8 — painting, photography, sculpture, digital art, mixed media and more. Submit up to 6 artworks via Google Form for free; fees apply only on acceptance, with discounted tiers for these volumes from $39 (full page) to $69 (double page) and $89 (exclusive interview or solo portfolio spotlight). Selected artists are featured in print with their portrait and artwork and promoted weekly for two months across the magazine's social media channels, with distribution to 83+ countries. — Deadline: June 15, 2026. Fee: Free ($39–$89 if accepted). Prize: Publication.

item.title: Bothy Project Residency — Sweeney's Bothy, Isle of Eigg · Visual Arts Scotland
item.description: Week-long residency at Sweeney's Bothy, a simple off-grid building on the Isle of Eigg in the Scottish Inner Hebrides, October 10–17, 2026, offered by Visual Arts Scotland with Bothy Project. Includes accommodation, a £720 artist fee and travel costs up to £250. Applicants must be VAS members at the time of application and residency. Apply by emailing written responses on practice, motivation, impact, documentation and sustainable travel plans (max 300 words each), completing the linked Google Form, and submitting a single PDF with 6 images of recent work. Cars are not permitted on the island; environmental sustainability is a selection consideration. — Deadline: June 14, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: £720 artist fee + £250 travel.

item.title: Fidra Fine Art Professional Members Exhibition · Visual Arts Scotland
item.description: Collaborative sales exhibition between Visual Arts Scotland and Fidra Fine Art, a contemporary gallery in Gullane, East Lothian, running October 17 – November 29, 2026. All mediums welcome. Selected artists show up to two works; a £15 hang fee is payable to VAS on selection and the gallery takes 40% commission on sales. Applicants must be VAS professional members for the duration of the exhibition. Apply by emailing a PDF with images of 6 works (titles, mediums, sizes, prices), a 200-word artist statement and CV, plus the accompanying Google Form. — Deadline: July 26, 2026. Fee: Free (£15 if selected). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Larnaca Biennale 2027 Open Call
item.description: Fifth edition of the Larnaca Biennale in Cyprus, October 13 – November 26, 2027, under the theme Metatopies: Geographies in Motion — place as an event in constant transformation, shaped by geological, anthropological, social, political and historical shifts. Curated by Niki Papaspirou and Marios Fournaris. Open worldwide to artists, photographers, designers and art students 18+, individually or in groups; material, technique and medium are open. Thirteen awards at the opening ceremony, including the Grand Prix, three awards of excellence and six awards of distinction. €50 fee per proposal for individuals (€75 for duos, €100 for groups of 3–5); submit up to three images per work with an optional 200-word statement. — Deadline: March 31, 2027. Fee: €50. Prize: Exhibition + Grand Prix + 12 awards.

item.title: Benjamin Hall Photography Award 2026 · Holt Art Projects
item.description: New award from Holt Art Projects — the team behind the Sir John Hurt Art Prize — celebrating photography as a way of seeing and engaging with the world. Open worldwide to any genre, analogue or digital; editing is allowed as long as the camera-made image remains central, but works built primarily in software are not eligible. Shortlisted works are exhibited in Holt, North Norfolk, July 20 – August 1, 2026, and the £1,000 winner is announced at the awards reception on July 19. — Deadline: June 14, 2026. Fee: £10–£25. Prize: £1,000 + Exhibition.

item.title: Next Generation RBSA 2026 · Royal Birmingham Society of Artists
item.description: Free early-career exhibition at the RBSA Gallery for recent graduates and self-taught artists living within easy reach of Birmingham. Submit 6–10 images of your current practice; shortlisted artists are interviewed in early August and selected artists exhibit September 1–12, 2026, receiving three years' free RBSA membership with automatic acceptance into two annual exhibitions and potential solo show opportunities. — Deadline: July 7, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: 3-year RBSA membership + Exhibition.

item.title: RBSA Prize 2026 · Royal Birmingham Society of Artists
item.description: Open-media exhibition of contemporary work at the RBSA Gallery in central Birmingham, with all styles and media eligible including photography. Up to four works per artist, selected anonymously from digital images. Prizes of £1,000, £500 and £250 plus up to six highly commended awards; the exhibition runs October 1–31, 2026. Open to local, national and international artists. — Deadline: August 11, 2026. Fee: £20–£48. Prize: £1,000 / £500 / £250.

item.title: Numéro+ Flux et Forma
item.description: Numéro Switzerland's open call on the theme Flux et Forma — flow and transformation, where constant change shapes creativity. Open worldwide to creators 18+, including photographers, videographers and multidisciplinary artists; submit a single project of images, video or both. The winner receives a print article and project cover feature in Numéro, digital promotion, a Nanlite lighting package and a copy of the magazine. — Deadline: October 25, 2026. Fee: €12. Prize: Publication + Cover feature.

item.title: San Francisco Photobook Fair 2026 · Harvey Milk Photo Center
item.description: The San Francisco Photobook Fair returns to the Harvey Milk Photo Center on October 17–18, 2026, following its first edition in 2025. Photobook publishers, individual artists, collectives and zine makers worldwide can apply for a table to display and sell image-forward publications — anything from zines and hand-bound books to folios, sculptural books and coffee-table titles. Accepted vendors are notified July 16; tables are $200 (full, wall access), $150 (full) or $75 (half), and limited scholarships for free or discounted tables are allocated based on need. Vendors handle their own sales and may also propose a talk or workshop for the event. — Deadline: June 19, 2026. Fee: Free (table $75–$200). Prize: Table at SF Photobook Fair.

item.title: Women Street Photographers Exhibition Call 2026
item.description: Annual exhibition call from Women Street Photographers, open to women and non-binary photographers of any age, anywhere in the world, using any camera or phone. Single images of street photography, street portraiture or abstract street photography made in public spaces are welcome. Thirty-four photographers are selected for an exhibition at the IPFIA gallery of the Centre Cívic Pati Llimona in Barcelona, November 5 – December 11, 2026, with printing and framing costs fully covered, publication across WSP platforms reaching over 200,000 followers, and a dedicated artist page on the WSP website. Free entries are available on request for photographers facing financial hardship. Deadline July 6, 2026, 6 PM New York time. — Deadline: July 6, 2026. Fee: $15/photo. Prize: Barcelona exhibition + Printing & framing covered.

item.title: InCadaqués Photo Festival Open Call 2026
item.description: Open call for the 10th edition of InCadaqués, the photography festival held in Salvador Dalí's village of Cadaqués on the Costa Brava. All photographers are welcome with a free-theme project of 10 to 15 photos; 20 projects are selected for exhibition during the festival. The grand prize winner receives €1,000 plus production costs, accommodation and transportation for the opening weekend; 14 finalists each receive €150 plus production of three exhibited images. Two further €1,000 awards — the Women Photography Award and the New Realities Award — and three €300 special mentions are also given. Results by the end of August 2026. — Deadline: July 17, 2026. Fee: €25. Prize: €1,000 + Exhibition.

item.title: God Is Dead — Premio BìFoto Fest 2026
item.description: Themed award of BìFoto Fest, the international photography festival of Sardinia, whose 16th edition opens in Mogoro on October 10, 2026. The theme draws on 'Dio è morto' (God is dead) by Italian band I Nomadi — a song that moves through disillusionment and loss while leaving room for hope. Open worldwide to photographers 18+, with projects of 8 to 12 photographs in any genre relating to the theme. Three winning projects are printed and exhibited at the festival, with accommodation and meals covered for the opening day and long-term visibility of the work. — Deadline: July 19, 2026. Fee: €25. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: APA Awards 2026
item.description: Annual awards of American Photographic Artists, the US trade association for professional photographers, aimed at commercial, editorial, entertainment and art photography. Fourteen single-image categories — from Architecture/Interiors and Beauty/Fashion to Documentary/Street, Personal Projects and FRESH/New Work — are judged blind, plus a separately judged Series category (2–6 images, $50 flat rate). Singles are $20–$30 for members and $50 for non-members. Winners are printed in the APA Awards book, with prizes including a Sony Alpha 7R V kit, Adobe Creative Cloud, Capture One, PhotoShelter and Think Tank items (prize delivery to US addresses only). Judging in July; winners notified by August. — Deadline: June 29, 2026. Fee: $20–$50. Prize: Printed awards book + Sony & Adobe prizes.

item.title: Earth Partner Prize 2026
item.description: Seventh annual prize from Earth Partner, the environmental initiative of artist agency Art Partner, presented in 2026 in collaboration with the Global Environment Facility (GEF) and Re:wild. Open free of charge to creatives aged 14 to 30 worldwide, responding to any aspect of the climate crisis — climate justice, conservation, indigenous rights, eco-anxiety, greenwashing and more — in any medium including photography and film. Submit up to 10 images or videos with a project description, short biography and a written reflection. Eight finalists receive cash prizes of $10,000, $5,000 or $2,000, with 20 honourable mentions and an Impact Award; the jury includes Hans Ulrich Obrist, Ferdinando Verderi, Shaway Yeh and Derrick O. Boateng. Deadline October 7, 2026, 23:59 CEST. — Deadline: October 7, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Up to $10,000 cash + 8 finalists awarded.

item.title: ProfiFoto New Talent Award 26/2
item.description: Second 2026 round of the New Talent Award from German photography magazine ProfiFoto, run in cooperation with Canon, WhiteWall and Hahnemühle for aspiring photographers who want to present their work to a professional audience. Submit a project concept (max. 2,000 characters) with 5 to 10 sample images reflecting your personal visual language — the call is open theme and open to any photographer. Winning works are published in ProfiFoto and shown as WhiteWall prints in a group exhibition; from the ten winning works across the year's two rounds, the jury selects the three best for cash prizes totaling €3,000. — Deadline: July 26, 2026. Fee: €20. Prize: Share of €3,000 + Publication + Exhibition.

item.title: Street Photography Barcelona Contest 2026 — 2nd Edition
item.description: Second edition of the Street Photography Barcelona Contest (SPBC), run by the team behind Ibizacinefest under the theme 'The Street Is Art'. Open worldwide to photographers 18+, with 1, 3 or 5 single images (€10/€25/€40) of spontaneous street photography taken in public spaces within the last two years — no AI or manipulated work, no journalistic photos or artificially lit portraits. Twenty-five finalists are exhibited at Galerie Art Nomade in Barcelona's Born district, November 6–9, 2026, with printing, framing and installation fully covered, and screened at Ibizacinefest in March 2027. Cash prizes of €500 (overall winner, including a flight and hotel to present in Ibiza) and two €250 special mentions are paid before the festival. Jury led by Xavi Herrero and Olivier Verdier. — Deadline: October 15, 2026. Fee: €10–€40. Prize: €500 + Exhibition.

item.title: Form Photo Award x UNSEEN
item.description: Open-theme round of the Form Photo Award from Form., the Paris-based multidisciplinary institution encompassing a gallery, magazine, publishing house and educational program. Open to professionals, amateurs and students of all nationalities over 18; black-and-white or colour work is accepted as single images or complete projects, with projects preferred for conveying the author's broader vision. Selected artists present their work in Form's exhibition at the UNSEEN 2027 photography fair. — Deadline: October 31, 2026. Fee: €35. Prize: Exhibition at UNSEEN 2027.

item.title: PhotoVogue Regional Open Call — MENA Panorama
item.description: PhotoVogue's regional open call dedicated to the Middle East and North Africa, following its Italian, Latin American, and East and Southeast Asian Panoramas. Open free of charge to artists 18+ from MENA and its diaspora, across photography, video and multimedia in all genres — fashion, documentary, portraiture, fine art and experimental. Submit a series of up to 15 images and/or a 60-second video trailer. Three artists receive $8,000 in total grants ($4,500 Outstanding Vision, $2,000 Vision, $1,500 Rising Voice); selected artists are featured at the 2027 PhotoVogue Festival, invited to PhotoVogue Virtual Portfolio Reviews, and considered for publication across Condé Nast titles in the region including Vogue, GQ, Architectural Digest and Condé Nast Traveler. AI-generated work is not accepted. — Deadline: September 24, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $8,000 in grants + Publication.

item.title: Road Trip Across America Photography Exhibition · City of Frisco Cultural Affairs
item.description: Photography exhibition from the City of Frisco's Cultural Affairs Division (Play Frisco) celebrating 250 years of American travel and landscapes, shown in the Grand Gallery of the Frisco Discovery Center. Open to Texas artists 18 and up with up to five photographs; submission is free, with a $30 entry fee due only if selected. Awards are announced at the public reception on July 11, 2026. — Deadline: June 15, 2026. Fee: Free ($30 if selected). Prize: Gallery exhibition + Awards at reception.

item.title: Photography — Your Vision · MVA Gallery
item.description: National juried exhibition at MVA Gallery (Modern Visual Arts) in historic Bethlehem, Pennsylvania, open to photography and photo collage of all styles and subjects with no restrictions. US residents 18+ may submit 3 to 9 images ($35 for three, $5 each additional). Awards include a $200 Director's Choice, an Art of Distinction award with a special exhibition, an honorable mention with free entry to a future show, and an annual grand prize of a New York City exhibition opportunity. Exhibition October 10 – November 7, 2026. — Deadline: June 15, 2026. Fee: $35 (3 images). Prize: $200 + NYC exhibition.

item.title: Hit Me With Your Best Shot! Bird Photography 2026 · Gallery by the Lake
item.description: Bird photography competition and exhibition from Gallery by the Lake, shown in the second-floor gallery of the Historic City Hall Arts & Cultural Center in Lake Charles, Louisiana. Open to photographers of all ages, amateur and professional, with birds from anywhere in the world as subjects; accepted works must be shipped from within the United States. Submit 5 to 8 images ($35 for five, $5 each additional). $1,325 in total awards: $450 Best in Show, plus $350/$100/$75 in the Open category and $250/$100 in the Restricted category. — Deadline: June 27, 2026. Fee: $35 (5 images). Prize: $450 Best in Show + $1,325 total awards.

item.title: National Juried Photography Exhibition 2026 · The Delaplaine Arts Center
item.description: National juried photography exhibition at the Delaplaine Arts Center in downtown Frederick, Maryland, on view November 7–29, 2026. Open nationally; work must be original in design and personal execution and created within the past two years. Awards are a $1,000 grand prize, $500 second place, $250 third place, and a $125 honorable mention. — Deadline: September 27, 2026. Fee: $35 ($25 members). Prize: $1,000 grand prize + Frederick MD exhibition.

item.title: TSHOW PHOTO.1 · Tyler Art Lift
item.description: First photography-dedicated edition of TSHOW, the international juried exhibition from Texas nonprofit Tyler Art Lift, created to highlight the diversity of contemporary photographic practice — traditional, experimental, documentary, conceptual, film and digital. Juried by Latvian fine art and fashion photographer Kristine Madjare, whose work has appeared in The New York Times, The Wall Street Journal and Financial Times. Exhibition at Gallery Main Street in Tyler, Texas, October 15–24, 2026, with cash prizes of $1,000 Best in Show, $500 runner-up and a $500 People's Choice chosen at the opening. Open internationally to artists 18+; $45 for the first entry, $5 each additional; 30% sales commission supports the show. — Deadline: September 7, 2026. Fee: $45 (1 work). Prize: $1,000 / $500 / $500.

item.title: Hamburg Portfolio Review 2026
item.description: Annual call from the Hamburg Portfolio Review, hosted by the FREELENS Foundation and supported by the Hamburg Ministry of Culture and Media and Canon Europe. A jury selects 100 photographers, who each meet one-on-one with up to 4 of more than 50 international reviewers — editors, publishers, curators, festival and museum professionals — in virtual sessions, and selected portfolios are also shown in exhibitions in Hamburg. Open to photographers over 18 worldwide; the focus is narrative photography rather than commercial or advertising imagery. Submit two projects of up to 10 images each or one project of up to 20 images. Free to enter; the 2026 deadline has been extended to June 14. — Deadline: June 14, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Expert portfolio reviews + Hamburg exhibition.

item.title: Bourse Photographe 2026 — Fondation Jean-Luc Lagardère
item.description: Annual €10,000 grant from the Fondation Jean-Luc Lagardère for a professional photographer aged 35 or under who wants to carry out a documentary photography production — in the social, economic, political or cultural field — in France or abroad. Applicants must already have published at least two documentary projects in the press, in a book or in an exhibition catalogue. The application dossier is submitted online and the project must be presented in French. Recent laureates include Marion Péhée, Aline Deschamps and Adrienne Surprenant. — Deadline: June 14, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €10,000 grant.
